title: Unsynced financial data is erased by a successful cloud refresh
repro: Intercept the accounts POST with 503; create through the real accountRepo; confirm the IndexedDB row; call accountRepo.list while the server still has no such row.
actual: Local row exists before refresh and disappears afterwards. Its failed outbox marker remains, but no durable payload/replay restores it.
impact: Shared repository behavior can silently discard financial writes after the UI accepted them. All cloud-mapped collections use this path.
fix: Persist a user-scoped payload-bearing outbox atomically with each local write; distinguish rejection from offline failure; merge cloud rows without deleting pending changes; implement retry and conflict handling.
test: Create/edit/delete offline, refresh, reload, restart browser, reconnect and reconcile one durable server row. Inject 401/403/422/500/timeout independently.

title: Concurrent retries can persist several entities for one mutation ID
repro: Send 24 simultaneous category creates with distinct entity IDs and one mutationId to a four-worker PHP server. Count persisted rows.
actual: Four distinct rows survived; expected one. Lookup occurs before the entity write and mutation-key insertion occurs afterwards.
impact: Exactly-once behavior is not guaranteed in the generic create path shared with transactions. The probe used categories, not a real payment; financial duplication is the shared-path risk.
fix: Claim the mutation key, write entity, effects and audit in one SQL transaction; bind the key to request hash and operation; return the original result for exact retries and reject changed payloads.
test: Concurrent retries with 1/4/16 workers, response loss, database failure, same key/different payload, same key/different collection and two different users.

title: Rejected sync batches leave partial financial writes
repro: Push two transaction rows: one valid expense followed by a negative-paise row. Read the first row after the 422 response.
actual: The request is rejected but the first row remains accessible with HTTP 200.
impact: A user can retry a failed import/sync without knowing part of it committed; cross-record invariants and totals can diverge.
fix: Validate the complete batch before writes and use an atomic transaction, or explicitly design and return per-row durable results with resumable keys.
test: Failure at every row and ledger/audit step must leave either all rows committed or an explicit, deterministic partial-result contract.

title: Stale sync data resurrects soft-deleted records
repro: Create a category, patch isDeleted=1, then sync the original older entity back.
actual: Sync returns 200 and isDeleted becomes 0. No version/tombstone conflict is enforced.
impact: Old devices can undo deletion or overwrite newer financial changes.
fix: Enforce expected versions and persistent tombstones; return conflict records instead of unconditional upserts.
test: Two-device edit/delete races, offline replay after deletion, clock skew, missing versions and intentional restore.

title: Collection hard-delete leaves posted SQL ledger events
repro: Create a transaction that produces a persisted financial event; DELETE its whole collection without an ids list.
actual: The collection rows are removed, but the existing financial_events count remains one.
impact: The SQL ledger can disagree with the visible transaction store, invalidating reports and repair assumptions.
fix: Route all removal paths through one transactional financial lifecycle with reversals or controlled purging and matching effects/audit updates.
test: Single, selected and whole-collection delete; rollback on event failure; assert no posted orphan event/effect.

title: Changing a PIN invalidates the configured recovery answer
repro: Set a security answer, change PIN with the correct current PIN, then submit the same answer for PIN reset.
actual: Reset returns 401. PIN salt rotated while the recovery answer remained hashed against the previous salt.
impact: Legitimate users lose recovery after an ordinary security operation.
fix: Use an independent password-hash salt for recovery, or migrate recovery safely during a verified change; do not couple recovery to PIN salt.
test: Set/change/reset/change sequences, repeated resets, wrong answers, Unicode normalization and recovery migration.

title: PIN changes and logout do not revoke bearer sessions
repro: Keep an issued bearer token, change the PIN, then log out. Call auth/me with the old token after each operation.
actual: Both old-token calls return 200. Logout clears the browser cookie but does not invalidate the token server-side.
impact: A stolen token remains useful after the user believes access was terminated.
fix: Add session records or a server-checked token/session version; revoke/rotate on PIN reset/change and logout; define all-device logout.
test: Old bearer and cookie tokens after change/reset/logout/admin reset/deactivation; active-session inventory and expiry boundaries.

title: Forced PIN rotation is not enforced for privileged access
repro: In the isolated database set admin must_change_pin=1 and call admin/users with its valid session. Restore the fixture flag afterwards.
actual: Privileged access remains allowed. The clean test seed also initially had must_change_pin=0 despite the documented default PIN.
impact: A seeded or administratively reset credential can retain full access without rotation. Not evidence that a public production admin still uses this PIN.
fix: Enforce the flag server-side for all operations except rotation/logout; add a blocking UI; avoid reusable production seed credentials.
test: First login, flagged existing session, direct API calls, all admin endpoints and every account reset route.

title: Recovery settings allow a session holder to replace the PIN without the existing PIN
repro: With a valid session, replace the security question/answer without currentPin, then reset the PIN with that new answer.
actual: Both operations succeed without the original PIN.
impact: Compromise of an unlocked session can become permanent credential takeover; the ordinary PIN-change currentPin check is bypassed.
fix: Require recent strong reauthentication for recovery changes and invalidate previous recovery material/sessions appropriately; audit and notify the owner.
test: Session-only recovery takeover attempt, stale reauthentication, PIN throttling, concurrent recovery replacement and legitimate reset.

title: CSRF enforcement is inconsistent across cookie-authenticated mutations
status: Reproduced server-side; browser exploit not demonstrated
repro: Send profile PATCH with sv_auth cookie, no CSRF header and an untrusted Origin. Compare sync push without CSRF.
actual: Profile mutation returns 200; sync push returns 403. Other generic/admin mutation wrappers also do not universally invoke the CSRF guard.
impact: Protection depends on endpoint and browser deployment. SameSite=Lax and CORS mitigate some cross-site attacks, so this probe alone is not proof of an end-to-end cross-site exploit.
fix: Centralize CSRF/Origin protection for cookie-authenticated writes; explicitly separate bearer-only clients; test the actual deployment origin and preflight behavior.
test: Same-site subdomain, cross-site fetch/form, absent/mismatched token, null Origin, strict CORS and bearer-only requests.

title: Spoofed forwarded IP addresses evade the login throttle
repro: Make seven wrong-PIN attempts for one username while changing X-Forwarded-For each time.
actual: All attempts return 401, never the intended lockout/rate-limit response. client_ip trusts forwarded headers without a trusted-proxy boundary.
impact: Short PIN credentials are vulnerable to distributed or header-rotating attempts; recovery endpoints also need dedicated throttling.
fix: Trust proxy headers only from configured proxies; combine account-level, source-level and global abuse limits with recovery controls.
test: Direct-origin spoofing, legitimate proxy chains, IPv6, distributed attempts, lock expiry, reset and denial-of-service resistance.

title: Household role restrictions can be bypassed through batch PATCH
repro: Create a viewer member and attempt role=owner with single-item PATCH, then with the collection batch PATCH.
actual: Single-item update is denied with 422; batch update succeeds with 200.
impact: Alternate mutation paths weaken permissions. Household roles are local per-user records, not proven multi-user agency roles.
fix: Resolve actual authenticated membership and enforce one authorization policy on create/single/batch/sync/delete paths.
test: Full owner/partner/viewer x operation x endpoint matrix including foreign households and membership removal.

title: Non-transaction collection contracts are not enforced as schemas
repro: Create a category with appliesTo=impossible and omit required presentation fields.
actual: HTTP 201 despite the generated contract declaring a constrained enum and required fields. Only transactions receive full domain validation.
impact: The 37-collection registry does not guarantee that stored data matches TypeScript assumptions; malformed records can propagate to UI and finance logic.
fix: Generate and execute validators for every collection and operation; reject unknown enums, missing fields and invalid version/relationship changes consistently.
test: Contract-derived positive and negative cases for all 37 collections, create/patch/batch/sync/import parity.

title: Full profile backup omits newer collections
repro: Build the full-export payload with household/card-EMI data in the current application context and inspect collection keys.
actual: The helper includes only 16 legacy collections; current household/card-EMI and other vNext data are absent.
impact: A successful-looking backup cannot restore the complete profile. Account data-export is a different server export and must not be conflated with this UI backup.
fix: Derive backup/restore coverage from versioned contracts; include dependencies and schema manifest; perform isolated round-trip verification before calling it full.
test: All 37 collections, deleted/tombstoned rows, cross-user isolation, attachment bytes versus metadata, legacy migrations and checksum comparisons.

title: CA workbook sheets use inconsistent period and ledger contexts
repro: Export only September transactions while passing August and September ledger events/effects, as ExportPage does. Also trace ReportsPage workbook invocation.
actual: September export includes August in monthly summary. ReportsPage supplies no events/effects, so ledger-derived sheets can be empty while master transactions exist.
impact: One workbook can contain contradictory financial periods or totals.
fix: Build a canonical report snapshot with a single period/time-zone policy and consistent linked event/effect sets; make both callers use it.
test: Identical exports from both entry points; opening/movement/closing handling; day/month/FY boundaries; no-data periods and refunds.

title: CA report helpers read noncanonical balance and Udhari fields
repro: Supply an account with openingBalancePaise=100000 and a payable Udhari with amount/settlement/givenDate fields from the canonical type.
actual: Net worth returns zero for the opening balance. Udhari ageing returns zero outstanding, given direction and zero days instead of 40000, received and 252.
impact: Asset/debt/ageing outputs can materially misstate the user position. Related debt helpers also use ad-hoc optional balance fields.
fix: Use typed canonical engines and settlement/effect data; eliminate cast-based alternate financial field names.
test: Opening-only accounts, receivable/payable partial settlement, card debt, loans, deleted rows and cross-report equality.

title: Some report totals ignore reversals and refunds
repro: Provide equal increase/decrease financing effects; export an expense of 100 with refund of 40.
actual: Financing cost becomes 20000 paise rather than zero; annual expense is 100 rather than net 60.
impact: Report definitions disagree with ledger lifecycle semantics and can overstate expenses.
fix: Use signed, status-aware canonical aggregates; name gross versus net values explicitly; share them across dashboard/report/export.
test: Full/partial refund, reversal-of-reversal, fees and tax reversal, refunded card expense, year boundary and raw/effect parity.

title: Reconciliation can report matched without an independent statement balance
repro: Generate account reconciliation when currentBalancePaise is absent from the supplied account.
actual: External balance defaults to the calculated closing balance, making variance zero and matched true by construction.
impact: A user or accountant can receive false assurance that books agree with a bank statement.
fix: Represent missing evidence as unverified; require an independently sourced dated statement balance and explicit match provenance.
test: Missing statement, real equal/different balances, period boundary, currency, duplicate imported statements and stale match invalidation.

title: Workbook business/personal summary ignores mixed allocations
repro: Export a 100 expense tagged mixed with 60 percent business allocation.
actual: Business and Personal rows remain zero; amount is only listed as Mixed. Expected allocated components are 60 and 40.
impact: The workbook split is inconsistent with the core split engine and unsuitable as a complete business/personal allocation.
fix: Use sumSplit on the same filtered lifecycle-aware transactions and expose unallocated totals distinctly.
test: 0/60/100 percent, explicit paise split, refunds, CSV/XLSX totals and comparison to report detail.

title: The reachable spreadsheet parser has high-severity advisories
status: Dependency advisory plus source reachability; no exploit executed
repro: Run npm audit --json and trace xlsx imports into the file-import page.
actual: Installed xlsx 0.18.5 is reported for prototype-pollution and ReDoS advisories with no npm-registry fix offered in that result.
impact: Untrusted spreadsheet parsing is a runtime surface; advisory presence is not proof of successful exploitation in this application.
fix: Choose a maintained upstream-supported distribution or replacement after compatibility review; add file/row/size/time limits and regression fixtures. Do not blindly run npm audit fix --force.
test: Representative bank workbooks, malicious/oversized/corrupt inputs, parse time budgets, formula cells and import-preview integrity.

title: Financial references are checked for presence but not existence
repro: Create an expense with nonempty accountId/categoryId values that do not exist.
actual: The server returns 201. A nonempty string passes validation without an owned referenced record.
impact: Orphan references can enter financial records via direct APIs; client-side refIntegrity does not protect backend writes or deletes. This is not evidence of reading a foreign account.
fix: Check owned, active referenced entities in the same transaction; enforce deletion dependencies and intentional historical-reference rules.
test: Missing, foreign-user, deleted and concurrently removed references for account/card/loan/goal/category/Udhari paths.

title: Backup restore breaks linked account and category references
status: Reproduced through the actual restore UI
repro: Import a JSON backup with one account, one category and a transaction linked to their original IDs; accept Continue restore; inspect persisted entities.
actual: UI reports Backup restored, but neither transaction accountId nor categoryId resolves. Restore discards entity IDs and generates new ones without a relationship map.
impact: A backup can restore rows while destroying financial meaning and balance attribution. This is independent of missing newer collections in B15.
fix: Build a two-pass old-to-new ID map, rewrite every foreign key/link, validate complete graphs and restore atomically with a preview and conflict policy.
test: Cross-profile and same-profile restore, repeated restore, all relationship types, cyclic links, partial failure and canonical checksum equality.

title: Wipe all profile data leaves newer profile collections behind
status: Reproduced through the actual Settings UI
repro: Create a household, use Wipe all profile data, enter the required DELETE username phrase, confirm, then GET the household.
actual: UI reports Profile data wiped, but the household still returns 200. Only 17 legacy repositories are cleared; the operation is a sequential partial wipe.
impact: The promised data removal is incomplete and may leave sensitive hidden data and orphan references. Separate account deletion is a different retained/soft-delete policy.
fix: Define wipe versus retained records explicitly; execute a server-controlled all-contract operation with reauthentication, audit and atomicity/recovery semantics.
test: All 37 collections, attachment bytes, local caches, outbox, failure halfway, cancel/wrong confirmation, account deletion distinction and documented retention.

title: The user-visible audit collection accepts fabricated records
repro: POST an invented action into the generic auditLogs collection.
actual: Server accepts it with 201. The user-facing audit trail is writable data. Separate SQL audit_logs/admin_audit_logs are not shown to be editable through this endpoint.
impact: Users or client bugs can create authoritative-looking history that must not be treated as immutable accounting evidence.
fix: Separate server-authoritative append-only audit from user activity annotations; expose a read-only authorized audit API and clear provenance.
test: Reject client audit mutation/deletion; verify actor, timestamp, before/after, correlation ID and transaction rollback semantics.

title: Oversized explicit mixed split can produce a negative component
repro: Set total=10000 paise and splitPersonalPaise=15000 without a business component.
actual: Business component becomes -5000. Valid percentage splitting does conserve totals across 14443 sampled cases.
impact: Malformed/imported data can create negative business spending even though total conservation alone passes.
fix: Reject negative/out-of-range component inputs and enforce nonnegative sum-equals-total invariants at API and UI boundaries.
test: Both explicit fields, one explicit field, zero/negative/noninteger/oversized amounts, percentages outside bounds and integer overflow.

title: Two loans with the same lender stop the CA export
repro: Export two active loans whose lender is Same Bank.
actual: Duplicate Amort_Same_Bank worksheet name throws. ExportPage caExport lacks try/finally and may remain in its exporting state.
impact: A common real profile cannot download the workbook; errors do not reliably recover the control.
fix: Generate deterministic unique sanitized sheet names and wrap all export steps in catch/finally with an actionable error.
test: Duplicate names, names equal after truncation/sanitization, blank names, >31 characters and repeated download after failure.

title: Excel master money cells are formatted strings
repro: Inspect the Amount cell in the generated Transactions_Master sheet.
actual: Cell type is s rather than n because currency formatting is applied before worksheet creation.
impact: Accountants cannot reliably sum/filter these cells as numeric money without cleanup; spreadsheet integrity is reduced.
fix: Write numeric rupee values with explicit number formats and preserve paise precision in machine-readable exports.
test: Parse saved workbook, assert numeric types/formats, SUM equality and locale-independent round-trip.

title: CSV export does not neutralize formula-like user text
status: Reproduced serialization; spreadsheet execution not tested
repro: Export a transaction description starting with =1+1 to CSV.
actual: Formula-like text remains in output. XLSX text-cell behavior is different and was not classified as the same vulnerability.
impact: Opening untrusted descriptions in a spreadsheet may interpret formulas. No external exfiltration payload was executed.
fix: Apply a documented spreadsheet-safe CSV text policy; preserve original values in JSON; test target spreadsheet behavior.
test: Leading =,+,-,@, whitespace/tab/newline and delimiter/quote combinations; Excel/LibreOffice opening tests with harmless payloads.

title: Development dependency security baseline is not clean
repro: Run npm audit --json against the current lockfile.
actual: 19 vulnerable dependency nodes: 4 critical, 7 high, 7 moderate, 1 low. Several are transitive development tooling; this is not 19 independent application exploits.
impact: Developer/CI attack surface and release maintenance risk remain. Vitest UI exposure is conditional and was not enabled in this audit.
fix: Update direct dependencies in reviewed groups with lockfile and build/test validation; separate runtime and dev exposure and record accepted exceptions.
test: Clean dependency scan, package integrity, scripts/build/coverage compatibility and dev server exposure tests.

title: Standard quality commands fail on metadata and environment assumptions
repro: Run npm run lint and the normal unit suite, then diagnostic runs excluding AppleDouble metadata.
actual: Normal lint has 279 parse errors. Clean unit run still has four failures: two missing .env.host fixtures and two Windows powershell invocations on macOS.
impact: The advertised quality gate is not reproducible on this machine. These are test/configuration failures, not evidence that 279 application files are broken.
fix: Ignore filesystem metadata in discovery and make secret/contract tests portable and self-contained; do not commit real secret files to satisfy tests.
test: Fresh checkout on macOS/Linux/Windows without private env files; stable suite counts and no secret leakage.

title: Several existing tests can pass without exercising the claimed behavior
repro: Review request setup and assertions for recovery, sync validation, account export, offline persistence and webhook replay.
actual: Validation cases receive CSRF 403 before schema checks; export fixture pushes fail silently; offline test stores only a marker; recovery browser test lacks success assertion; replay fixture username exceeds VARCHAR(20).
impact: Green log lines overstate business-flow assurance. Extra probe X05 confirms a correctly seeded own-data server export succeeds.
fix: Assert fixture creation before assertions, expected status/code/body and final durable state; test real offline financial writes; fix fixture bounds.
test: Each formerly false-positive test must fail against the known defect and pass after a scoped fix; avoid click-only success.

title: Shared form labels and several icon controls lack accessible names
repro: Inspect Field markup and scan visible interactive elements in mobile views.
actual: Field renders a sibling Label without htmlFor/input id linkage. Profile scan found 20 unnamed-control candidates; category actions and account icon buttons add more.
impact: Screen-reader/form navigation is impaired. The heuristic scan is not a full accessibility conformance assessment.
fix: Generate stable field IDs, associate label/hint/error, provide aria-invalid and explicit button names; test keyboard/focus semantics.
test: Axe plus manual VoiceOver, keyboard-only dialog flows, label activation and error announcements on desktop/mobile.

title: Mobile navigation omits Categories and Audit
repro: At 390px inspect the bottom navigation and all command palette route buttons.
actual: Neither Go to Categories nor Go to Audit is present; desktop sidebar includes both. Direct URL navigation still works.
impact: Users on mobile lose discoverable access to important data-management and audit features.
fix: Derive mobile More menu and palette from the canonical authorized route registry; include all accessible routes with predictable grouping.
test: Every allowed route reachable without typing URLs at 360-430px; hidden/paid/admin routes handled correctly.

title: The initial application bundle is large and largely unsplit
status: Measured build; user latency not benchmarked
repro: Run the production Vite build and inspect emitted assets and chunk warnings.
actual: Main JS is 2099.49 kB, gzip 620.68 kB; 3453 modules transformed. Static and dynamic imports overlap.
impact: Parsing and first-load cost may be substantial on low-end/mobile networks; no numeric latency claim is made without profiling.
fix: Introduce route-level lazy chunks and defer spreadsheet/chart tooling, then profile before further optimization.
test: Lighthouse/Web Vitals and CPU/network traces on representative devices; no route blank states or asset-loading regressions.

title: The PHP development router serves repository internals
repro: GET /.git/HEAD, /package.json and /src/App.tsx from the audit PHP server rooted at the repository.
actual: All return 200. .env and sql/schema.sql return 403. The production packaging allowlist excludes most source/git files.
impact: Exposing this development server or deploying the raw root would reveal source/history. Public production exposure was not tested or established.
fix: Keep dev servers loopback-only; deny dotfiles and source paths; deploy only the reviewed build artifact and test actual hosting rules.
test: Forbidden paths and encoded variants against PHP dev and Apache staging; no git/source/secret/backup downloads.

title: Authorization and unexpected errors use misleading/raw 500 responses
repro: Call admin/users as a normal active user; inspect wrapper catch behavior.
actual: Access is denied but returned as 500 rather than 403. Generic wrappers can return raw exception text.
impact: Clients cannot distinguish permission from server failure, monitoring is noisy and database errors may expose internals. No cross-user read succeeded in this probe.
fix: Use typed central error mapping with safe messages, request IDs and server-only detailed logs.
test: 401/403/404/409/422/429/500 contracts, malformed JSON, database outage and sensitive-string suppression.

title: Concurrent default seeding creates duplicate accounts/categories
status: Observed browser fixture; source race confirmed
repro: Register a fresh user in the development build; inspect initial accounts before and after one manual account creation.
actual: There are two each of Cash, Savings Bank and UPI Wallet, plus the one manually added account. Seed functions use check-empty then non-idempotent creates; StrictMode/concurrent initialization can race.
impact: New profiles begin with duplicate containers/categories; two tabs can cause the same class of race outside StrictMode. Exact multi-tab production reproduction remains pending.
fix: Make seeding server-side atomic/idempotent with stable unique seed identities; deduplicate only with a reviewed migration preserving references.
test: StrictMode mount, rapid login/reload, two tabs and concurrent first-login calls must create exactly one default set.

title: Export description lists the wrong workbook sheet count
repro: Compare CA Workbook description with a downloaded empty-profile workbook.
actual: UI says Includes 16 sheets; download contains 21 sheets, plus possible per-loan sheets.
impact: The export description is stale and obscures what is actually delivered.
fix: Generate the section list/count from the workbook definition; describe conditional sheets.
test: UI list, downloaded manifest and conditional loan sheet counts remain consistent.

title: Seed branding/contact content remains placeholder-like
status: Observed test seed and source; production content unverified
repro: Open seeded admin branding settings and inspect the configured contact/legal values and placeholders.
actual: support@example.com is present in the test configuration; logo/favicon inputs show example URLs as placeholders.
impact: Sample contact content should not be shipped as real company support information. Input placeholders themselves are not defects.
fix: Provide deployment-validated real support/legal/branding settings and distinguish placeholders from persisted values.
test: Staging content review, valid legal pages and support links; no production example addresses.
